gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the common '2000W/200W' dual-outlet travel converters the '200W' outlet does not convert voltage at all and passes 220–240 V straight through. It also doesn't state that the '2000W' outlet runs only heating appliances and AC-motor hair dryers with mechanical switches, never Dyson, DC-motor or digital dryers. Meanwhile the 200–300 W single-mode converters, the type ChatGPT showed (Ceptics 200W, TESSAN 250W), ban hair dryers whatever their wattage. So the wattage in the name tells you neither what gets converted nor what can be plugged in.
standout_why: Compared against ChatGPT's answer, globalplugs.com/blog/voltage-converter-vs-adapter, voltwander.com/faq and doace.com adapter-vs-converter-vs-transformer. ChatGPT only says compact converters 'cannot safely handle' hair dryers. Globalplugs covers continuous vs surge ratings but has nothing on dual outlets, pass-through outlets or Dyson. Voltwander only says a dryer needs '2000W+'. Doace mentions pass-through sockets only for USB-C plug adapters and names a 2000 W converter without its limits. None says that a converter's own '200W' outlet does not convert. I could not read the text of the cited manuals.plus PDFs (TESSAN TC02, TESSAN TUS-2, the other TESSAN, FOVAL) or the Digital Camera World Ceptics review. That is why I scored 2 rather than 3.
decides: It splits the pick by device. (1) For a 110 V-only electronic device or small heated tool up to about 200–300 W, buy a single-mode converter whose outlets all convert: TESSAN TC03 (250 W max), Ceptics PU-200C, BESTEK 250W/300W, or BESTEK 200W pure sine for curling irons and straighteners. Never use the '200W' socket on a 2000W/200W unit for a 110 V-only device, because that socket puts out wall voltage. (2) For a 110 V-only hair dryer with a mechanical switch, the '2000W' outlet on a dual-outlet unit works (Ceptics LX-C2000 or LX2-M2000 at $49.99, BESTEK 2000W EU at $50.99). (3) For a Dyson or other electronic-control dryer, only the Ceptics VC-S2000 pure sine model ($129.99) names Dyson as supported, and only with nothing else plugged in. The TESSAN TC03 we already list is the right pick for electronics only.
